title: fleetlint catalog
description: A catalog of rules: presets select from the library, organisations and teams publish their own. See https://fleetlint.org/writing-rules/.

includes.description: Catalogs this one builds on, loaded first: fleetlint:<preset> or pinned remote references.

engine.description: The engine level the catalog was written for.

label.description: Who owns the catalog (`org`, `team/mobile`, `security-team`): the name reports attribute its rules and policy to, and a name for `--require`. It does not order catalogs. Default: the sources-file name the catalog is loaded under, else its own name.

layer.description: Deprecated spelling of label, still read.

catalog.description: The fleetlint catalog version this repository runs with (presets, library and fix templates): a tag or a full commit SHA, and the repository when it is not fleetlint/catalog. One version holds for a run; a sources file may set it for every repository.

version.description: A tag or a full commit SHA of the catalog repository. A commit cannot move; a tag can.

repo.description: The catalog repository (https or ssh). Default: https://github.com/fleetlint/catalog.git

oci.description: The catalog version as a published artifact: <registry>/<repository>:<tag>, optionally @sha256:<digest> (ghcr.io/fleetlint/catalog:v0.1.0). Instead of version and repo. A tag of ghcr.io/fleetlint/catalog is verified against the catalog repository's signature; any other tag needs signers in the sources file, a digest needs none.

overrides.description: Adjustments to rules the catalogs brought in, keyed by rule id or a pattern over ids ("*", "release/*"); patterns apply first. The repository adjusts: severity (lowering needs a reason), raise, params, accept, enabled with a reason. Policy keys (locked, min_severity, exceptions) and applicability (when, tiers) are set by catalogs.

reason.description: Required when disabling a rule or lowering its severity.

raise.description: Lift the severity this many steps, capped at error.

when.description: Replaces the rule's when; "true" makes a conditional rule unconditional.

tiers.description: Replaces the tiers the rule applies to.

locked.description: Later layers cannot disable the rule, lower its severity or redefine it.

min_severity.description: The lowest severity a later layer may set.

exceptions.description: false forbids per-finding exceptions to the rule.

match.description: Glob against the finding's path, or re:<regex> against its message. Omit to cover every finding of the rule.

until.description: YYYY-MM-DD; after this date the finding returns at full severity.

rules.description: The repository's own rules, in the catalog format: full definitions with an id, or `use: <id or glob>` entries that select library rules. A rule a catalog already defines cannot be redefined here; adjust it under overrides.

use.description: Select a library rule or a family (lint/*); no other keys.

id.description: family/name; family/name/<stack> implements the capability family/name for one stack (or `any`).

refs.description: Where the rule's practice comes from: a URL, or {url, kind, section}. Kinds, strongest first: spec, guidance, style-guide, standard, check (section is the linter's check id), convention (no outside source).

since.description: The catalog version that added the rule.

by.description: On a capability: what its implementations are keyed by. `stack` (the default): rules/<family>/<name>/<stack>.yaml, one per detected stack. `artifact`: rules/<family>/<name>/<artifact>.yaml, one per published artifact kind from the catalog's artifacts/, checked for every kind the release publishes.

combine.description: On a capability: whether every implementation that runs in a scope must pass (all, the default) or one passing is enough (any, for what belongs to the repository rather than to each stack, such as a release).

locked.description: Later layers cannot disable the rule, lower its severity or redefine it.

min_severity.description: The lowest severity a later layer may set.

exceptions.description: false forbids per-finding exceptions to the rule.
